findings.title: math.attention() computes avg-pool + self-gate, not self-attention
findings.quote:
def attention(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, pe: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    q, k = apply_rope(q, k, pe)
    channels = rearrange(v, "B H L D -> (B H) D L")
    local = F.avg_pool1d(channels, kernel_size=7, stride=1, padding=3)
    local = rearrange(local, "(B H) D L -> B H L D", B=v.shape[0], H=v.shape[1])
    gate = torch.sigmoid((q * k).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True) / math.sqrt(q.shape[-1]))
    mixed = gate * v + (1.0 - gate) * local
    return rearrange(mixed, "B H L D -> B L (H D)")
findings.claim: The function named `attention` (called by every DoubleStreamBlock at layers.py:185) applies RoPE and computes a per-token self-score q_i·k_i, then returns gate*v + (1-gate)*avgpool7(v) — a local moving average of values gated by each token's self-similarity. It never forms the QK^T token-by-token matrix and never softmaxes, so there is no cross-token attention.
findings.concern: The 19 DoubleStreamBlocks that feed the extracted FLUX feature (block 28) are run with this operator instead of the scaled-dot-product attention the pretrained FLUX weights were trained for, so the extracted 'FLUX features' are not FLUX features; every reported DiTF_flux number is affected. _audit_code shows cosine≈0.13 / rel-L2≈3.1 vs real SDPA (which the SingleStreamBlocks DO use at math.py:32, exposing the inconsistency).
findings.resolution: Confirm whether the numbers in Tables 2–4 were produced with this `attention` body or with standard `scaled_dot_product_attention`; if the latter, restore the upstream FLUX attention (q,k=apply_rope; x=F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q,k,v)).
findings.reason: src/flux/math.py:7-14 exactly matches the quoted body; verifier script independently confirms cosine_similarity≈0.1254 and rel-L2≈3.10 vs real SDPA, proving the function is not scaled-dot-product attention.

findings.title: load_flow_model opens ./results/flux/metrics.json, which is absent → crash on startup
findings.quote:
ckpt_path = configs[name].ckpt_path
with open("./results/flux/metrics.json") as stream:
    metrics = json.load(stream)
selected = max(metrics.values(), key=lambda item: item["point"]["All"])
ckpt_path = selected["checkpoint"]
findings.claim: Every run enters Featurizer.__init__ -> load_flow_model('flux-dev'), which unconditionally opens ./results/flux/metrics.json. No results/ directory or metrics.json exists anywhere in the repo (verified by find).
findings.concern: The evaluation cannot start: FLUX loading raises FileNotFoundError before any image is processed, so nothing in the repo is runnable as shipped.
findings.resolution: Remove the metrics.json lookup (the upstream loader just uses configs[name].ckpt_path or hf_hub_download), or ship the metrics.json the code expects and document how it is produced.
findings.paper_ref: NeurIPS checklist Q5 (code available with instructions)
findings.reason: util.py:125-128 exactly matches the quote; find across the entire repo returns no results/ directory or metrics.json file, confirming the crash condition.

findings.title: chunk(2) unpack in eval_spair.py crashes under the shipped --ensemble_size 1
findings.quote:
feat_pred_uncond, feat_pred_text = src_ft_raw.chunk(2)
# src_ft_raw = feat_pred_uncond + guidance_scale * (feat_pred_text - feat_pred_uncond)
src_ft_raw = feat_pred_text
findings.claim: Saved features have batch dim = ensemble_size (feat_flux.py:149; the averaging `mean(0)` is commented out at feat_flux.py:197). test_spair.sh ships `--ensemble_size 1`, so src_ft_raw has batch 1 and torch.chunk(x,2) returns ONE chunk; the 2-tuple unpack raises ValueError.
findings.concern: The shipped reproduction command (test_spair.sh) crashes at the matching step; _audit_code confirms `chunk(2)` on a batch-1 tensor gives 1 chunk -> 'not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)'. (The argparse default --ensemble_size 8 happens to be even and avoids it, but then the 8 members are never averaged and only member 0 is used.)
findings.resolution: Either drop the uncond/text chunk (the CFG combine is commented out and unused) or document that ensemble_size must be even; align test_spair.sh accordingly.
findings.reason: eval_spair.py:175-177 exactly matches the quote; test_spair.sh ships --ensemble_size 1; verifier script confirms chunk(2) on a batch-1 tensor returns 1 chunk and raises ValueError: not enough values to unpack.

findings.topic: model selection on the test set
findings.title: Model checkpoint is selected by maximising the SPair test-set PCK
findings.quote:
with open("./results/flux/metrics.json") as stream:
    metrics = json.load(stream)
selected = max(metrics.values(), key=lambda item: item["point"]["All"])
ckpt_path = selected["checkpoint"]
findings.claim: Setting aside the missing file, the loader chooses the checkpoint that maximises item['point']['All'] — the per-point PCK@0.1 that eval_spair.py computes and writes for the SPair-71k *test* split (results/<model>/<gs>.json). i.e. the model/config is picked by its score on the evaluation set.
findings.concern: Selecting the checkpoint/config that scores highest on the test set is selection-on-test: for a training-free method with no validation split, this optimistically biases the reported PCK. There is no val/train split anywhere to select on.
findings.resolution: Authors: clarify what metrics.json contained and whether any reported number used max-over-test selection; select on a held-out validation split (or a fixed config) instead.
findings.reason: util.py:125-128 matches; eval_spair.py hardcodes test_path='PairAnnotation/test' (test split) and writes result['point']['All'] — exactly the metric util.py maximises; confirmed test-set-based checkpoint selection.

findings.title: Only the FLUX backbone is implemented; SD3, SD3-5, Pixart-α absent
findings.claim: `--dift_model` is gated to 'flux' only (choices=['flux'] at eval_spair.py:314; raises otherwise). No feature extractor exists for SD3, SD3-5, or Pixart-α; the repo has no code path for them.
findings.concern: The DiTF_sd3-5 rows in Tables 2 and 3, all of Table 5 (conditions ablation across Pixart/SD3/SD3-5/Flux), and the per-backbone Figure 6 curves cannot be reproduced — including the paper's SOTA claim, which is carried by DiTF_sd3-5† (72.2 on SPair).
findings.resolution: Release the SD3, SD3-5, and Pixart-α feature-extraction code, or restate the results as FLUX-only.
findings.reason: eval_spair.py:100-103 and :314 exactly match the quote; choices=['flux'] and the else-raise confirm only FLUX is implemented; no other backbone code exists in the repo.

findings.title: DINOv2-fusion (the † SOTA rows) is not implemented anywhere
findings.quote: Integration of DINOv2 feature. We extracted DINOv2 features from the token facet of the 11th
findings.claim: The paper's best numbers are the † variants that concatenate DiT features with DINOv2 (Appendix C: 11th-layer token facet + channel-concat + pairwise PCA to 1280). No DINOv2 model is loaded and no such concat exists in the repo (grep for 'dino' finds only a local variable name in an unused PCA helper).
findings.concern: Every † row in Tables 2 and 3 — including the headline SOTA (DiTF_sd3-5† 72.2 on SPair, +2.6% claim; the AP-10K SOTA rows) — has no code and cannot be reproduced.
findings.resolution: Release the DINOv2 loading + feature-fusion + pairwise-PCA code used for the † results.
findings.paper_ref: Appendix C 'Integration of DINOv2 feature'; Tables 2, 3 († rows)
findings.reason: Paper text line 1686 confirms the quote; grep across all .py files finds 'dino' only as the local variable cat_desc_dino in a generic PCA helper — no DINOv2 model loading or feature-concatenation code exists.

findings.title: Channel-discard strategy (a named contribution) is absent from the code
findings.quote: their influence. Specifically, we zero out the corresponding dimensions of these weakly massive
findings.claim: Channel discard — zeroing the dimensions of weakly-massive activations in the post-AdaLN feature (§4.3) — is one of the paper's four contributions and the final ablation step. The eval pipeline applies only (1+scale)*LayerNorm(feat)+shift (eval_spair.py:190) and never zeroes any channel (grep for discard/zero/topk/argsort: none).
findings.concern: The '+ Channel discard' row of Table 4 and the headline DiTF_flux SPair number (67.1) cannot be produced; the shipped code yields at most the '+ AdaLN' value (~65.3 in Table 4).
findings.resolution: Release the channel-discard implementation (which dimensions, how selected) so Table 4's last row and the headline number are reproducible.
findings.reason: Paper text lines 415-417 confirm the quote; grep for discard/zero_out/topk/argsort across all .py files returns nothing; eval_spair.py:190 applies only (1+scale)*ft+shift with no channel zeroing.

findings.title: AP-10K and PF-Pascal evaluation code absent
findings.quote: correspondence, and temporal correspondence. For semantic correspondence, we conduct experiments on three popular benchmarks: SPair-71k [57], PF-Pascal [58], AP-10K benchmark [43]. The
findings.claim: The repo ships only a SPair-71k evaluator. There is no loader/evaluator for PF-Pascal or the AP-10K intra-/cross-species/cross-family benchmark.
findings.concern: The AP-10K columns of Table 3 (including the abstract's '+4.4% on AP-10K-C.S.' and the '4.8% (64.6->69.4)' cross-species claim) and the PF-Pascal columns cannot be reproduced from the code.
findings.resolution: Release the AP-10K and PF-Pascal evaluation harnesses (data loaders, pair lists, PCK-per-image computation).
findings.reason: Paper text line 779 confirms the quote; the repo root contains only eval_spair.py with no AP-10K or PF-Pascal loaders, and choices=['flux'] with a single SPair test path.

findings.title: Segmentation, HPatches, DAVIS, and all massive-activation analyses have no code
findings.claim: No code exists for: ADE20K segmentation head/eval (Table 6), HPatches homography (Table 8), DAVIS temporal correspondence (Table 9), the massive-activation variance analysis (Table 1), the activation/pre-vs-post-AdaLN visualizations (Figures 2–5, 10–16), or the block-index/timestep grid search (Figure 12).
findings.concern: None of the paper's secondary quantitative results or its central diagnostic evidence for the 'massive activations' phenomenon can be reproduced or verified from the repository.
findings.resolution: Release the analysis and secondary-task scripts, or scope the release statement to what is provided.
findings.reason: Paper text line 899 confirms the quote; the repo contains only eval_spair.py and src/flux/ — no ADE20K, HPatches, DAVIS, or analysis scripts exist anywhere.

findings.title: No README, no dependency spec, and a placeholder dataset path
findings.quote: Justification: Datasets and codes are available for double-blind review in the supplementary
findings.claim: The checklist claims code+data with sufficient reproduction instructions, but the repo has no README, no requirements.txt/setup.py/pyproject.toml (only a stale upstream `flux.egg-info` that omits diffusers, scikit-learn, scipy, opencv-python, matplotlib, seaborn — all imported by the eval code), and test_spair.sh hardcodes a non-existent dataset path `spair-71k_path` and model paths under `./hg_models/`.
findings.concern: A reader cannot rebuild the environment or point the script at data without reverse-engineering imports and paths; there is no results table + exact command to reproduce any number.
findings.resolution: Add a README with exact commands and expected numbers, a pinned dependency list covering the added imports, and dataset/model download+placement instructions.
findings.reason: Paper text line 1239 confirms the quote; find finds no README, requirements.txt, setup.py, or pyproject.toml in the repo; test_spair.sh uses literal placeholder 'spair-71k_path'.

findings.title: Shipped input resolution is 768×768, paper states 960×960 for DiTs
findings.quote: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 python eval_spair.py --dataset spair --dataset_path spair-71k_path --save_path dfm_feats/spair_flux_img768 --dift_model flux --img_size 768 768 --t 260 --ft_index 28 --ensemble_size 1
findings.claim: The shipped run uses --img_size 768 768 (and eval_spair.py's argparse default is [512,512]), whereas Appendix C states the DiT input size is 960×960.
findings.concern: Feature-map resolution affects PCK; reproducing the paper's exact numbers may require 960×960, which the shipped command does not use. Valid-but-different setting, so a difference rather than a defect.
findings.resolution: State the exact input resolution used for the FLUX SPair numbers and align test_spair.sh with it.
findings.paper_ref: Appendix C: 'set the input image size as 960x960 for DiTs'
findings.reason: test_spair.sh line 1 exactly matches the quote (768 768); paper_text.txt line 1677 confirms '960x960 for DiTs'; the mismatch is real.
